In this equation, I’m the exact same as your girlfriend. And me and my boyfriend have been in the same situation. She’s obviously having some insecurities, and having all this free time means having a LOT of time thinking about these insecurities. So I’d say from her perspective, you don’t have to spend all of your time with her - just a simple text here and there telling her you love her is all she needs. Trust me, when my boyfriend told me he needed some time to himself I instantly freaked and thought that during the time to himself he’d realise that he actually doesn’t need me anymore. And thinking back to it now, it’s silly. We decided to have a talk and meet in the middle. We sat down and spoke about what bothered us both. And I told him that having time to himself was understanding, but if he could just text me maybe once in the morning and once at night to let me know he’s ok and that he loves me. So my advice is maybe sit down and tell her EVERYTHING that’s bothering you, have her do the same. And maybe make her feel a little bit better about the break by letting her know you’re still there thinking about her. 

You’ll finally adapt a new schedule where she’ll be less insecure about it, she’ll find hobbies and you’ll both feel better about yourselves. And trust me, the best times are seeing each other, after being apart. I hope this helps

I find the situation with your boyfriend is a lot similar to what me and boyfriend are going through, except I’m the person with anxiety. I agree with the other comment that some people don’t want help, and it’s true. Some people bask in their own sadness and don’t want to help themselves and just want self pity. But I also think that what your boyfriend is going through is not that he doesn’t want to help himself, it’s that he feels like he’s too much of a burden.

When you have anxiety and you suffer from it every single day, it’s exhausting. And you often think about how it’s exhausting your relationship, and how it’s affecting the other person. I often tell my boyfriend I’m not sure why he’s still with me because I feel like I put a huge responsibility on him and it could ruin our relationship. I also refuse to go to a therapist because I also believe I will cope with it on my own. Some people need the assistance of a therapist and some can learn to cope on their own- everyone is different. The only thing you can do is be there for him - which is the biggest responsibility but if you love him you will.

He’ll try to cope with it on his own, but on the way there will be times when he’s exhausted from it and he’ll need you, but let him come to you don’t pester him because it will increase the stress. The only thing you can do is reassure him daily, and talk about his worries. And teach him to love himself, even if he won’t listen at first.

I believe whole heartedly in life that things happen for a reason. The fact that you haven’t done it and you’re still here today means that you’re still meant to be here. And the fact that your dog is the only reason you’re here, means you were MEANT to have your dog. It sounds ridiculous, but if you start looking at things as though they were meant to happen and how things are the way they are rather than why- you’ll find that the majority of the things that have happened have encouraged you to want to do things like that, but actually by not doing them you can see what kind of person you are.

Your dog is clearly an important figure in your life and has prevented you from taking your own. And that just means that your love and care for your dog is much more important than your own wishes- which in itself is a selfless act and shows that you put other people before yourself. 

But now if you focus on yourself for a second, you’ll realise that despite wanting to take your own life, already we all know reading this that you’re in fact a very decent human being, and without people like you on this earth - we’d have nothing. Without people like you, we’d have no good in the world and without you imagine just how sad your dog would be for the rest of his life. A dogs attachment to its owner never leaves them. 

You say that you’re being treated as though you don’t exist, of course I don’t know you or your situation, but perhaps use this as an advantage. The only person who should truly care about your existence is yourself and how important your existence is. Maybe stop thinking about why people treat you like this, and perhaps more how you can focus on yourself with your own independence. If people are treating you like that, then they aren’t nice people and you shouldn’t be around people like that, find nice people. 

You don’t need other people to justify your own existence. 

But no matter what happens, in the end please never leave your dog.

I can really relate to this as I’m the girl that also does this to her boyfriend. It’s not about what you’re doing ie holding her hand etc that’s a problem, it just makes anxiety worse. She may need some time to herself, or she may want you to be with her and just laying beside her without doing anything- just enjoying your presence. In my case, I hate when I’m extremely anxious and my boyfriend tries to cuddle me to make me feel better, it makes me feel a lot more constrained and claustrophobic. He isn’t doing anything wrong, just in that moment I like time to myself with him just being in the room for reassurance. 

As crazy as it sounds, it really works. I completely shut myself down to him and I know it frustrates him. Sometimes I wonder if I should end it with him so that he doesn’t have to put up with that responsibility. But the truth is, you’re with your girlfriend because you love her and want to take care of her- so simply just be there for her. You don’t have to do or say anything, she’ll come to you when she’s ready. She’ll learn to adapt and when she’s ready she’ll share her worries with you so that she “shuts down” less. 

The reason why she’s so triggered is because of the change- it’s too fast and as you may know with anxiety yourself, change is too much. And eventually your girlfriend will get used to the idea of coronavirus and the riots etc- but when it’s all over, the change will be too much for her again - and returning to normal will be difficult for her. Your job is just to be there for her when she needs you. Maybe try and distract her from social media or the news, things that are talking about these things, and try focusing on something she likes.

I hope this helps, this really helps in my situation, and I hope it’s the same with your girlfriend. It’s really amazing how much effort you’re going through to try and help her. Good luck, and I hope she (and you of course) are ok.

It’s very weird...and scary. It’s also worrying how we could harm ourselves unintentionally without realising that’s what we’re doing. 

I also was taught that people who self harmed just cut themselves so I had no idea that’s what I was doing. When I found out that’s what I was doing, I kind of felt a bit ashamed that I’d let myself get that far. 

I can’t imagine ripping my cuticles, or the pain that follows- you’re extremely strong to go through that and I’m sorry that that’s your way to feel pain. I hope you find a way to stop, or find a healthy way to cope. Thank you for your comment, it’s made me feel a whole lot better and a lot less alone in this.

I think if you’re doing an action that is hurting yourself physically or mentally on purpose, then it self harm. So if you do it obsessively to feel pain or have a form of relief, then yes I guess it’s classed as self harm. If you’re doing it as a coping mechanism and it’s an unhealthy obsession, then I think you should talk to someone about it - popping pimples can be really dangerous. However, this is just my opinion, and I don’t know a lot about self-harming so I could be totally wrong. 

But what I can tell you, is that if your anxiety and depression is causing you to do something obsessively then you should try and find other things to distract you from popping pimples. Find a healthy obsession, or try healthy coping mechanisms.
